This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. The Petitioner apprehending eviction of his Tiffin Stall has filed this writ petition seeking for a direction to allow him to continue his business in the place, where his Tiffin Stall is operating.

3. Mr. Mohapatra, learned counsel submits that the Petitioner was issued with a Food Safety &
Standards Authority of India Certificate by the Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Odisha on 16th January, 2021 (Annexure-1), which was valid till 15th January, 2022.

sentences.text:
The Petitioner is running such Tiffin Stall at Railway Station Square, Unit-III, Kharavela Nagar,
Bhubaneswar.
The case of the Petitioner was recommended by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India to avail the benefit under PMSVA Nidhi Scheme.

entities.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Petitioner made an application on 21st March, 2024 in the prescribed format to issue street vending license in his favour, which is yet to be considered.
Hence, this writ petition has been filed for the aforesaid relief.

Ms. Prajna Priyambada, learned counsel for Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation submits that no such application has yet been received by the Town Vending Committee of Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC).

entities.text: Town Vending Committee of Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Copy of the said application annexed to the writ petition as Annexure-2 does not bear any signature in token of receipt of such application.
Although the application is stated to have been filed on 21st March, 2024, immediately thereafter the writ petition has been filed on 23rd March, 2024.
The Petitioner has no locus standi to be issued with a street vending license.

Hence,
the writ petition being devoid of any merit should be dismissed.

5. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court feels that if the Petitioner intends to get vending certificate under the provisions of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 and the Rules framed thereunder, he should make a fresh application in that regard enclosing relevant documents and information.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Accordingly, this Court without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case of the Petitioner for being issued with a vending certificate, disposes of this writ petition with a direction that in the event the Petitioner makes a fresh application under the provisions of the aforesaid Act and Rules within a period of two weeks along with relevant information and documents, the same shall be considered as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of one month therefrom and decision thereof shall be communicated to the Petitioner forthwith.
Till disposal of the aforesaid application, if filed within the time stipulated, as above, status quo with regard to continuance of the business of the Petitioner shall be maintained.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
(K.R. Mohapatra)
Judge  (S.K.Mishra)
